summary:
FireStorm turns decades of NASA microgravity combustion research into fire-safety decisions for future lunar and Martian habitats.                   
                                                                                                                                                                                    
 The app ranks NASA investigations by how closely their conditions match the habitat, how many safety domains they cover and how much data they hold. It forecasts whether a    
  material will burn by combining two models. A scikit-learn neural network (MLP), trained on oxygen, pressure and airflow, covers the ISS microgravity conditions it was trained   
  on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
  A gap map shows where NASA has test data and where it has none, and recommends the next experiment where data is missing, the habitat is affected and the model is most uncertain.
  The models flag every forecast that goes beyond tested conditions.                                                                                                                
     A natural-language Copilot answers questions with interactive widgets backed by NASA citations.
details: Project Impact: To accelerate and optimize microgravity combustion safety research by providing engineers with instant, explainable, and offline-capable physics forecasting tools that flag data gaps, guide targeted funding experiments, and replace days of manual NASA report analysis. OFFLINE MODEL ONNX AND GENUI WITH FLUTTER
